verses.pali: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yatthimā mahānadiyo saṁsandanti samenti, seyyathidaṁ—
verses.english: “Mendicants, there are places where the great rivers—the Ganges, Yamunā, Aciravatī, Sarabhū, and Mahī—join together and converge.

verses.pali: gaṅgā yamunā aciravatī sarabhū mahī, tato puriso dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni uddhareyya.
verses.english: Suppose a person was to draw two or three drops of water from such a place.

verses.pali: katamaṁ nu kho bahutaraṁ, yāni vā dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni ubbhatāni yaṁ vā sambhejjaudakan”ti?
verses.english: Which is more: the two or three drops drawn out or the water in the confluence?”
“Sir, the water in the confluence is certainly more.

verses.pali: appamattakāni dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni ubbhatāni.
verses.english: The two or three drops drawn out are tiny.

verses.pali: Neva satimaṁ kalaṁ upenti na sahassimaṁ kalaṁ upenti na satasahassimaṁ kalaṁ upenti sambhejjaudakaṁ upanidhāya dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni ubbhatānī”ti.
verses.english: Compared to the water in the confluence, it’s not nearly a hundredth, a thousandth, or a hundred thousandth part.”
“In the same way, for a noble disciple, the suffering that’s over and done with is more …”
